c.st: Is reality a computer simulation? Does it matter?
c.x: Obviously this is a theme that has been explored in SF a fair amount (recent examples include Ken Macleod's The Restoration Game and Iain Banks' Surface Detail). One obvious problem is that it appears to be highly immoral to generate a simulation in which millions or billions of sentient beings suffer, which presumably would weigh heavier on a more advanced species (human or otherwise).

c.st: Alan Watts Predicted LLM Usage in 1951
c.x:
While reading Alan Watts' book The Wisdom of Insecurity (published in 1951), I noticed that he predicted the rise of something akin to large language models with eerie accuracy.

It is interesting to me that the same feeling of societal dread (the first chapter is called "The Age of Anxiety") is still relevant 75 years later, with the very issue that Watts predicted on p. 69 being front and center in our news cycles.

c.st: Why I don't think AGI is imminent
c.x:
One of the most impactful books I ever read was Alvin Toffler's Future Shock.

Its core thesis was: Every era doubled the amount of technological change of the prior era in one half the time.

At the time he wrote the book in 1970, he was making the point that the pace of technological change had, for the first time in human history, rendered the knowledge of society's elders - previously the holders of all valuable information - irrelevant.

The pace of change has continued to steadily increase in the ensuing 55…
